# {{PROJECT_NAME}}

A CLI and authenticated HTTP application for Cortex backend-owned runs. The installed backend owns Agent/Workflow orchestration, governed inference, tool approvals, context, transcript and memory stages. The application sends only new user text and immutable run identifiers.

## Setup

Use the modern `cortex init` setup or `cortex backend --help` to inspect the additive installer and verified development provisioning helper. Install into the host's configured functions directory; retain its custom schema, auth and HTTP router. Ambiguous merges must be resolved before installation. Provision a published Agent definition, current host-JWT membership/grants, and qualified Gateway policies in the backend. No OpenAI, Anthropic or Gateway inference key belongs in this application.

Copy `.env.local.example` to `.env.local`, configure the existing deployment and published Agent, and obtain a JWT from your host authentication service. Tenant/space labels are selectors; the backend verifies identity and access. For CLI refresh, point `CORTEX_AUTH_TOKEN_FILE` at a host-managed private UTF-8 token file (`chmod 600`). The callback rereads it for every official refresh. A process-only `CORTEX_AUTH_TOKEN` is also supported. Tokens are never printed. HTTP always requires the caller's own Bearer JWT and never uses the CLI token.

The additive setup's `NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_CORTEX_AGENT_ID`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_CORTEX_AGENT_VERSION` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_CORTEX_MEMORY_SPACE_ID` selectors are supported. Explicit `CONVEX_URL`, `AGENT_ID`, `AGENT_VERSION` and `MEMORY_SPACE_ID` values take precedence.

```sh
npm install --ignore-scripts
npm run build     # Offline TypeScript; does not deploy
npm start         # CLI
npm run server    # Loopback HTTP application
npm run dev       # Watch the application only; no Convex/Docker startup
```

Backend installation/deployment and optional graph workers are separate operator tasks. `build:convex` is an explicit deploy command and must only run against an authorized target. Graph synchronization requires the registered durable outbox, scoped service JWT and configured Node connector; graph lag is distinct from memory readiness. Private assets require the additive authenticated HTTP routes, enforce 20,000,000 bytes, and use immutable asset/version selectors. Media generation needs a genuine qualified model envelope and budget; unavailable async video remains unavailable. The Basic app does not store generated bytes, guess profiles or run another tool/model loop.

## CLI

Plain text creates and prints one request ID, admits the run, then displays its streamed and canonical final answer through the same client. It pauses at explicit approval or terminal completion. `/send <requestId> <text>` returns the handle for later observation with a caller-chosen stable ID. An ambiguous response is never retried automatically; keep the original request/run ID. Ctrl+C releases local observation and the client; use `/cancel` to ask the backend to cancel.

- `/observe [runId]` reads the current durable output; `/watch [runId]` observes until terminal/approval or the configured local deadline.
- `/approve-input [runId]` approves input; `/approve-tool <operationId> <toolName> <requestHash>` uses the exact displayed server request hash for the current run.
- `/cancel [runId]` requests server cancellation. Closing an observation only disconnects locally.
- `/recall <requestId> <query>` performs a governed retrieval, independently of chat.
- `/history`, `/conversations`, `/profile`, `/readiness`, `/session`, `/new`, `/exit` expose fresh verified metadata/history. Session changes fail closed.

Response completion can precede facts/vectors/graph readiness. A published strict Agent definition controls its barrier; a status read does not change that policy. `PROFILE_NOT_READY`, `CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE`, `POLICY_DENIED`, `FORBIDDEN` and deadline/unknown outcomes are actionable errors, not echo-mode success.

Optional title work follows canonical answer finalization. For local diagnosis, set
`CORTEX_RUNTIME_LATENCY_TRACE=1` to emit metadata timings for client RPCs and the
submission-to-first-printed-answer boundary. Enable the same flag separately on an
authorized backend for its context, model-policy and Gateway phases. These diagnostics
do not contain prompts, reply text or credentials. The under-one-second first-visible
target requires actual installed-client measurements; it is not a service guarantee.

## HTTP

All functional routes require `Authorization: Bearer <host JWT>`, return `Cache-Control: no-store`, and allocate a scoped client with `finally` cleanup. There is no wildcard CORS, ambient authenticated singleton or private request/error logging. JSON bodies are capped at 32 KiB and five seconds; text is capped at 16 KiB. Runtime work defaults to a 30-second local deadline (1..120,000 ms); timeout closes local observation, not upstream work or its financial liability.

```sh
curl http://127.0.0.1:3001/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HOST_JWT" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"requestId":"caller-stable-1","message":"Hello"}'
```

`POST /chat` returns 202 with a verified handle and run status. Continue with `GET /runs/:id`, `GET /runs/:id/observe`, `POST /runs/:id/start`, `POST /runs/:id/cancel`, or input/tool approval endpoints. Observation cursor resume uses both `cursor` and `attemptNumber`; a nonzero cursor without its attempt is rejected. Use `POST /recall` with `{requestId,query}`, `GET /history/:id?cursor=...`, `/conversations`, `/profile` and `/readiness`. `/health` exposes only application health, without private scope metadata.

## Checks

`npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:unit` and `npm run test:integration` are offline. Unit tests cover auth/configuration bounds, connection lifecycle, stable submit/observe, exact approvals and cancellation. Integration tests invoke the actual Hono application with a controlled remote client and enforce no paid effects before validation.

`npm run test:e2e` is a separate, explicit service check. Provide a verified disposable development target, current host token, tenant/space/Agent configuration and `CORTEX_E2E_TARGET_VERIFIED=true`. Bind existing completed owned `CORTEX_E2E_RUN_ID` plus optional loopback `API_URL` for unpaid installed read/recall-readiness checks. The tests never provision, deploy, purge or invoke paid models just to become green. Missing prerequisites fail clearly; offline success does not certify actual backend/media/graph behavior. Native installation and authenticated runtime/browser evidence remain separately required for the full integration task.
